subject: maths
pattern: Probability carries about 6-9 marks: 1/2-mark items on conditional probability and independent events, a 3-mark total probability or Bayes problem, a 3-mark probability distribution or binomial problem, and sometimes a 5-mark Bayes theorem statement and proof or a binomial distribution derivation. Always write the formula first, then substitute.

questions.answer: The probability of occurrence of event $A$ given that $B$ has already occurred is $P(A|B)=\frac{P(A\cap B)}{P(B)}$, where $P(B)\ne0$.

questions.q: If $A$ and $B$ are independent events with $P(A)=0.3$ and $P(B)=0.4$, find $P(A\cap B)$.
Write the mean and variance of the binomial distribution $B(n,p)$.
A fair coin is tossed three times. Find the probability of at least two heads given that the first toss is a head.
questions.answer: Given first toss head: outcomes HHH, HHT, HTH, HTT (4 equally likely). At least two heads: HHH, HHT, HTH (3). Probability $=\frac34$.

questions.q: Find the mean of the number of heads in two tosses of a coin.
Two cards are drawn successively without replacement from a pack of 52 cards. Find the probability distribution of the number of aces and its mean.
Bag A has 3 red and 5 black balls; bag B has 6 red and 4 black balls. A bag is chosen at random and a ball drawn. Find the probability that it is red.
questions.answer: By the theorem of total probability: $P(R)=P(A)P(R|A)+P(B)P(R|B)=\frac12\cdot\frac38+\frac12\cdot\frac6{10}=\frac3{16}+\frac3{10}=\frac{39}{80}$.

questions.q: Machines $A,B,C$ produce 25%, 35% and 40% of items, with 5%, 4% and 2% defective respectively. An item chosen at random is defective. Find the probability that it was produced by $C$.
A die is thrown 4 times. Find the probability of getting at most 2 sixes.

questions.answer: Statement: If $E_1,E_2,\dots,E_n$ are mutually exclusive and exhaustive events with $P(E_i)>0$ and $A$ is any event with $P(A)>0$, then $P(E_i|A)=\frac{P(E_i)P(A|E_i)}{\sum_{j=1}^nP(E_j)P(A|E_j)}$. Proof: $P(E_i|A)=\frac{P(E_i\cap A)}{P(A)}$. By multiplication rule $P(E_i\cap A)=P(E_i)P(A|E_i)$. By the theorem of total probability $P(A)=\sum_j P(E_j)P(A|E_j)$. Substituting gives the result.

questions.q: Derive the probability of exactly $r$ successes in $n$ Bernoulli trials, $P(X=r)={}^nC_r\,p^rq^{n-r}$.
questions.answer: Each trial has success probability $p$ and failure $q=1-p$, trials independent. One particular sequence with $r$ successes and $n-r$ failures (e.g. $SS\dots S\,FF\dots F$) has probability $p^rq^{n-r}$ by independence. The $r$ successes can occupy any $r$ of the $n$ places in ${}^nC_r$ ways, all mutually exclusive with equal probability. Hence $P(X=r)={}^nC_r\,p^rq^{n-r}$, $r=0,1,\dots,n$. These terms are those of $(q+p)^n$, whose sum is 1.
